attempted_claim: Let A,B be unital separable simple nuclear Z-stable C*-algebras with tracial rank TR(A),TR(B) <= 1, where neither algebra has real rank zero nor unique trace. Suppose there exist an invertible kappa in KK(A,B) with kappa_0([1_A])=[1_B] and an affine homeomorphism gamma: T(B) -> T(A) satisfying <gamma(tau),x> = <tau,kappa_0(x)> for all tau in T(B), x in K_0(A). Does it follow that A is isomorphic to B without assuming the UCT for A,B and without assuming (kappa,gamma) is induced by a *-homomorphism?
decisive_failure: The UCT-free step could not be closed: neither a UCT-free classification or homomorphism-realization theorem nor a non-UCT counterexample in this class is available, and both coincide with the open UCT problem beyond the scope of a bounded pass.
